text: Civil/architecture engineering cleaning investigation: building cooling load in kW. Raw synthetic operating records are retained unchanged. The file has 91 records including one duplicate record_id. I keep its first occurrence so a repeated upload does not double-count demand. One target is missing, so I exclude that row because the response cannot be inferred honestly. One load is -5 percent, outside the physical 0–100 percent range, so I exclude that row instead of clipping it. One ambient temperature is missing; after excluding invalid records I fill it with the retained observed median. This robust imputation limits the influence of unusually hot readings. I make copies and do not overwrite the raw CSV. The clean result has 88 observations, all IDs unique, targets present and load within 0–100. The target mean is 46.641159 kW. The counts reconcile: 91 minus one duplicate minus two invalid rows is 88. One temperature is imputed; no other values change. I assert ID uniqueness and target completeness after cleaning, and compare input values before and after to confirm the raw list is intact. The data quality statement is that these are synthetic teaching records, not measured buildings. The remaining limitations include a small sample, repeated observations per equipment and one imputed temperature whose uncertainty is not represented. This cleaned table is suitable for practicing summarization, not sizing a real cooling system. Before engineering use we need measured, calibrated observations from representative buildings and operating conditions.

These are synthetic building cooling-load observations in kW. They are suitable only for teaching, not real deployment. Repeated equipment observations are not independent and the sample is small. More representative measured buildings and calibrated sensors would be needed. I did not identify defects or reconcile row counts.
